jobs.title: Research Analyst
jobs.location: Kampala, Uganda GROSS SALARY RANGE: $2, 979 - $4, 092(gross monthly) Laterite is looking for a new Research Analyst with an understanding of data analysis and a strong motivation to work in social and economic research to join our office in Kampala, Uganda. This role combines research design, data analysis, project management support, data quality analysis, and fieldwork coordination in a collaborative and fast-paced environment. WHO WE ARE Laterite is a data, research, and analytics firm working on complex development challenges. We partner with universities, global think tanks, international NGOs, multilateral donors, and government ministries. Our clients include the World Bank, TechnoServe, the Mastercard Foundation, and others. We operate across the Netherlands, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and Peru, with 90+ full-time staff and more than 2, 000 enumerators. We believe meaningful impact requires being on the ground, building local teams, and establishing long-term trust. Our office culture is collaborative and gives people autonomy to grow into their roles. THE ENVIRONMENT YOU’RE STEPPING INTO You will join our team in Uganda in a high-trust environment. We are low on bureaucracy but high on individual accountability. You won’t be micromanaged here—we want you to use your judgment to solve problems, support our fast-paced field teams, and actively improve the systems you work with. Laterite was founded in 2010 in Kigali, and our office in Kampala opened in 2018. Our project portfolio in Uganda is varied across multiple sectors, and ranges from data collection studies, where Laterite manages data collection for our clients, to full-cycle research projects, where Laterite is responsible for evaluation and sampling methodology, survey design and coding, data collection, data quality and analysis. The Uganda team has managed some of our largest data collection projects and phone surveys on topics spanning coffee agronomy, foundational learning and education, sexual and reproductive health, and renewable energy. Our team in Uganda currently consists of 5 team members. TEAM STRUCTURE You will report to the Research Manager and Uganda country lead, working closely with the research operations team and data quality colleagues across Laterite. You will have the opportunity to collaborate with research team members in other country offices HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT 1 Supporting research projects Support the ethical approval process, research design, and development of research instruments, Conduct quantitative and qualitative data analysis. Draft sections of reports and presentations for clients. Support communication with clients and internal project teams on project progress. 2 Contributing to data collection Code survey instruments using SurveyCTO and other ODK-based platforms. Collaborate with field teams to develop training materials and support enumerator trainings. Participate in field visits to understand and improve data collection processes. 3 Strengthening data quality and analysis Monitor, clean, and validate incoming survey data (by conducting high-frequency checks, for example). Work closely with field teams to resolve data quality issues. Support statistical analysis and interpretation of findings. Contribute to consultancy-quality reports and data-driven insights. 4 Contributing to business development (Optional) If you are interested, there is also room to contribute to our business development efforts, either through proactive business development or by contributing to the development of technical and financial proposals. WHAT YOU BRING We are looking for a colleague with strong quantitative data analysis skills and a motivation to work on socio-economic development research. Specifically, you have: A completed Master’s degree in Economics, Public Health, Development, statistics, or related fields. At least one year of professional experience in similar roles or tasks. (We welcome experience gained through internships, dissertation work, or participation in an academic research group, provided you can demonstrate how this experience meets the requirements of the role.) Strong quantitative data analysis skills and proficiency in Stata. Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. In addition, we welcome: Experience working with ODK-based platforms (e.g., SurveyCTO). Previous work experience in Uganda Additional software skills, such as knowledge of R or Python. Organizational and interpersonal skills, self-motivation and drive to work in a collaborative environment. WHAT YOU’LL LEARN AND DEVELOP Technical research design, including sampling and impact evaluation methodologies. Project management and client communication. Advanced data analysis, statistical techniques, and coding skills. Report writing and presentation of findings in a consultancy-quality format. WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU Competitive compensation. $2, 092 gross monthly salary (exact grade determined by experience/interviews), medical insurance, pension contribution, and 21 days of annual leave. Professional growth. We are also committed to supporting our staff’s learning, providing an annual learning budget of up to $1, 000 per person and 10 days of time off for professional learning each year. Flexibility. We also provide remote work options in accordance with Laterite’s remote work policy. How to apply READY TO BUILD WITH US? NEXT STEPS Online assessment. Complete a 30-minute online verbal reasoning and quantitative assessment. No special preparation is required. Link: https://form.jotformeu.com/262993195544571 Application. Candidates who successfully complete the online assessment will be invited to submit a brief screening questionnaire, along with their CV, through our online application system. Analytical assessment. Selected candidates will complete a technical exercise involving statistical analysis using Stata, R, or Python. Interviews. Candidates who successfully complete the analytical assessment will be invited to a first interview. The interview stage consists of up to two interviews.

jobs.title: Technical Advisor II – Climate Change & Landscape Restoration
jobs.location: Kampala This position is open to Ugandan nationals only Deadline: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm. Job Summary You will provide strategic technical leadership, advice, guidance, and support across program design, business development, implementation, learning, and evidence generation in the areas of Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration. Working in line with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) program quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices, you will support Country Office(CO) teams to develop, implement, and scale innovative, high-quality programming that advances resilience, environmental stewardship, and sustainable livelihoods for poor and vulnerable communities. Your technical knowledge, advice and guidance will contribute to determining how effective, adaptive and innovative CRS’ Climate Change and Landscape Restoration programming is across Uganda. Your technical expertise, strategic vision, and leadership will contribute to the growth and positioning of CRS Uganda's Climate Change and Landscape Restoration portfolio. You will help identify and pursue new funding opportunities, lead technical design for priority investments and proposals, build relationships and partnerships, and support the effective implementation of strategic initiatives that generate evidence, demonstrate impact, and inform future programming. Through collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, you will strengthen CRS' reputation as a trusted partner and technical leader in climate resilience, nature-based solutions, and landscape restoration across Uganda. Roles and Key Responsibilities Contribute to the development and implementation of CRS Uganda strategies, standards, tools, and best practices in Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration that effectively engage partners, donors and governments. Help ensure a cross-sectoral approach integrating gender, protection mainstreaming, and disaster risk reduction, while promoting innovation, and evidence-based programming. Provide technical solutions to CP teams, remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and how to best apply program design and implementation standards, best practices, partnership principles, and M&E, ensuring high-quality implementation. Support adaptive management and the use of evidence and learning to strengthen program quality and impact. Lead CRS Uganda's technical efforts to position and grow its Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration portfolio by identifying emerging opportunities, strengthening strategic partnerships, and shaping innovative, evidence-based programming approaches. Lead or contribute to the technical design of large and/or complex proposals, including the development of technical strategies, theories of change, and appropriate monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks in collaboration with business development, MEAL, and other cross-functional teams. Advise project teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities, and technical requirements into CRS' approach and support the development of programming that strengthens CRS' competitiveness, impact, and thought leadership. Lead the design, and technical oversight of strategic initiatives and discretionary-funded investments in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration that generate evidence, strengthen partnerships, and inform future programming and resource mobilization efforts. Contribute to technical communications, visibility, and thought leadership efforts by supporting the development of success stories, case studies, presentations, publications, learning products, and other materials that showcase CRS' experience, evidence, and impact in Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration. Contribute to capacity strengthening initiatives in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration programming for staff and partners through helping develop learning and training strategies and agendas/curriculums, conducting trainings and workshops, and mentoring and coaching. Contribute to knowledge management and learning through collecting and analyzing program data, evaluating strategic projects, assisting with measuring program impact, capturing and sharing lessons learned and best practices, and research and internal reports. Establish and maintain relationships with donors, peer organizations, research and other institutions. Participate in forums in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration to collect and share best practices and promote CRS’ work, support organizational positioning, and identify opportunities for collaboration and resource mobilization. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s Degree in Climate Change, Forestry, Agroforestry, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, Ecology, Environmental Management, Agriculture, or a related field required. Minimum of eight years relevant international working experience in an advisory or management role with progressive responsibilities, ideally with an international NGO, with minimum of three years working for programming interventions in climate change adaptation and mitigation and/or landscape restoration Previous experience providing technical assistance and developing successful proposals for external donor funding is required. Preferred Qualifications Master's Degree in Climate Change, or a related field is an advantage Demonstrated ability to convene, coordinate, and facilitate complex multi-stakeholder consultations and partnerships involving government, development partners, technical agencies, academia, and community stakeholders. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Demonstrated application of technical principles and concepts in climate change adaptation and mitigation and landscape restoration. General knowledge of other related disciplines to ensure a proper cross-sectoral approach. Proficient in MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information and budget management systems, knowledge-sharing networks. Experience in business development, project design and proposal development in, including technical writing. Experience in mentoring, coaching, facilitation and training applying adult learning principles and practices. Experience with program monitoring and evaluation, including applying data collection tools and methodologies, data analysis, and data presentation. Experience and skills in networking and relations with donors, and faith-based civil society partners. Understanding of partnership principles. Excellent relationship management skills with ability to influence and get buy-in from people not under direct supervision and to work with individuals in diverse geographical and cultural settings. Strong strategic, analytical, problem-solving and systems thinking skills with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment Strong written and oral communication skills Strong presentation, facilitation, training, mentoring, and coaching skills Proactive, resourceful and results-oriented Required Languages - Fluent English is required. Working proficiency in local language is a plus. Travel - include percentage of required travel, if applicable. Could be stated as Must be willing and able to travel up to 30 %. Supervisory Responsibilities: No Key Working Relationships: Internal: CRS Country Representative, Head of Programs, Head of Operations, Uganda-based technical experts for MEAL, Emergency focal point, Gender, Youth and Social Inclusion (GYSI) and Partner Capacity Strengthening (PCS), Regional and Headquarters technical staff. External: Local partner staff, representatives from for-profit and other non-profit organizations and relevant national, district, sub-county, parish and other government stakeholders, community leaders. Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff): Personal Accountability – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions. Acts with Integrity - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest. Builds and Maintains Trust - Shows consistency between words and actions. Collaborates with Others – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams. Open to Learn – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things. Agency Leadership Competencies: Lead Change – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation. Develops and Recognizes Others – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance. Strategic Mindset – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities. jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst for Ethiopia, based in Kampala
jobs.location: Kampala, with possible travel to Addis Ababa Starting Date : ASAP. COUNTRY PROFILE Since 2018, Ethiopia has experienced escalating insecurity and unrest, including large-scale displacement, loss of life, and widespread destruction of property, following significant domestic political changes. These crises have compounded the effects of recurring climate-related shocks affecting large parts of the country. In November 2020, conflict erupted in the northern Tigray region, triggering significant displacement across Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions. Since August 2023, renewed conflict in Amhara has further intensified humanitarian needs, leading to the declaration of a state of emergency and restrictions on movement across the region. Together, these crises have severely disrupted livelihoods, constrained access to essential goods and staple commodities, and increased the vulnerability of affected populations, placing additional pressure on humanitarian response capacities across the country. JOB PROFILE The Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist position is based in Kampala, with possible travel to Addis Ababa. The position is fully dedicated to the Ethiopia mission and will report directly to the Deputy Country Representative. The postholder will lead the mission’s data team, coordinating its work across the Sectoral, Intersectoral and PANDA units in close collaboration with Research Managers, the GIS Specialist and relevant HQ technical teams. The postholder will provide technical leadership and backstopping throughout the research cycle, from methodology and sampling design to data collection, cleaning, analysis, validation and dissemination. The role is responsible for coordinating data officers and interns, agreeing priorities and resource needs with Research Managers, maintaining reusable analysis systems, and ensuring compliance with IMPACT research standards and data protection requirements. The appointment level will depend on the selected candidate’s experience and technical skills, both profiles will carry responsibility for leading the data team. During the assignment, the Senior Data Analyst / Data Specialist will be hosted by Acted, IMPACT's global partner, and will be under the responsibility of its delegates for all administrative, security, logistics and financial matters. The postholder will fully comply with Acted and IMPACT rules and procedures, including those relating to data protection and information security. RESPONSIBILITIES Planning and coordination: Estimate deadlines and resource requirements for each research cycle across the Sectoral, Intersectoral and PANDA units. Coordinate team members’ workloads, agree data team priorities with Research Managers, and flag risks, capacity gaps and delays early, in writing, to the relevant Research Managers and direct manager. Research design: Support assessment teams in designing methodologies, sampling strategies (including sample size calculations and survey weighting), data analysis plans and data collection tools, in line with IMPACT research standards. Data collection and cleaning: Oversee the review, testing and deployment of XLSForms on IMPACT’s Kobo server, data checks during collection, and data cleaning in line with IMPACT’s Data Cleaning Minimum Standards. Where relevant, train enumerators and partner staff on data checks and cleaning. Analysis systems: Maintain and develop the mission’s R-based cleaning and analysis workflows, including IMPACT R packages, templates and Shiny applications, under version control and with up-to-date documentation so that they can be reused across research cycles. Information products: Review country-level information products and dissemination strategies to maximise the use of findings, in accordance with IMPACT research standards and in close coordination with the direct manager. Data quality: Improve data quality and monitoring at country level, including resolving discrepancies, keeping geospatial and administrative reference data up to date in coordination with GIS colleagues, and ensuring collected data is correctly georeferenced. Data protection: Ensure compliance with IMPACT’s data protection policy and SOP on personally identifiable information in all research cycles. This includes anonymisation and disclosure-risk checks before any dataset is shared, secure transfer, storage and deletion of data, and compliance with data-sharing or data processing agreements with partners. Capacity building: Lead the development and implementation of an ongoing capacity-building plan for country data officers and interns, with support from relevant technical colleagues and HQ teams. Provide training, mentoring and regular feedback on data cleaning, analysis and tools, and coordinate with Research Managers on staff development and performance. Partner engagement: At the request of the line manager, support partners on data processing, data sharing and the use of findings, and represent IMPACT on data matters in relevant coordination forums. DELIVERABLES Lead weekly data team meetings, maintain a shared task tracker with clear responsibilities and agreed timelines, and follow up on progress and outstanding actions. Provide technical guidance to data officers and interns on cleaning, analysis and troubleshooting, implement and track the capacity-building plan, and provide input to their performance appraisals in coordination with Research Managers. Regularly liaise with project focal points and Research Managers to monitor deadlines and resource needs, anticipate delays, and communicate risks and agreed corrective actions in writing. Conduct internal technical validation of all research cycles, including review of sampling, data collection tools, cleaning and analysis outputs, to ensure alignment with IMPACT/HQ guidelines before submission to HQ for validation. Ensure regular maintenance of all mission dashboards, including Power BI and Shiny, and contribute to the design and development of new dashboards when required. Keep documentation, including READMEs, SOPs and decision logs, up to date for all workflows and dashboards maintained by the data team, with code under version control and clear maintenance responsibilities. For every dataset shared outside IMPACT, document the anonymisation applied, disclosure-risk checks and transfer, in line with the relevant agreement and applicable IMPACT procedures. REQUIRED SKILLSET At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in data management and analysis, preferably in humanitarian settings. A master’s degree in a relevant discipline, such as statistics, data science or social sciences, is preferred. Fluency in English is required. Excellent communication and data visualisation skills. Strong skills in R and in data cleaning and survey analysis workflows, familiarity with IMPACT’s R packages is an asset. Proven skills in Power BI and R Shiny. Experience with KoboToolbox or ODK and XLSForm design. Sound knowledge of sampling methods, sample size calculations and survey weighting. Experience with Git/GitHub, GIS skills in QGIS or ArcGIS are an asset. Knowledge of humanitarian data protection practice, including anonymisation of microdata and disclosure-risk assessment. Experience supervising or mentoring data staff, including remotely. Ability to manage multiple priorities across many research cycles, at times under tight deadlines. Strong ability to work independently in support of colleagues and partners. Ability to work in an intercultural environment. Previous experience in Ethiopia or the Horn of Africa is highly preferred. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere. Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse. Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance. Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered). Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance) Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable. Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training, IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees. How to apply Please apply directly on the website via the following link: Senior Data Analyst for Ethiopia, based in Kampala (External Applicants), Impact

jobs.title: Senior Project Officer - Communications
jobs.location: Kampala This position is open to Ugandan nationals only . Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm. Job Summary The Senior Project Officer - Communications will lead the development and production of high-quality, audience-focused communications products that showcase the impact, lessons learned, and successes of CRS Uganda's programs. Working closely with project teams, local partners, and participants, this role will package these insights for donors and stakeholders, ultimately advancing CRS' mission to serve the poor and vulnerable. The Senior Project Officer - Communications will work proactively with CRS project technical teams and local partners to identify, gather content and produce case studies, success stories, videos, photos, social media content and learning pieces. You will also develop content production calendars that align with program implementation cycles and document the full story of project implementation and the transformative journey of project participants. The Senior Project Officer – Communications will coordinate with CRS country, regional, and global communications and marketing teams to enhance the visibility of projects among diverse audiences. In this role, your skills and knowledge will help ensure the delivery of high-quality communications products that effectively support project objectives and strengthen program impact. The Senior Project Officer - Communications works closely with the Country Program leadership team and Regional Marketing Strategist to create content and ensure strategic alignment of communications, consistent messaging, and a strong brand identity. The Senior Project Officer - Communications creates content and uses effective communication channels to reach diverse audiences and help strengthen CRS Uganda's positioning for funding and influence. This includes stories, multimedia, reports, and other communications materials as required, while ensuring compliance with CRS and donor branding and marking requirements. Roles and Key Responsibilities Capture high-quality photography, videography, interviews, and testimonials directly from the field to showcase the impact of CRS Uganda's programs. Collaborate closely with project teams, and project participants to maintain a consistent, active pipeline of human-interest stories and multimedia assets. Write, design, and produce creative visibility materials, including project fact sheets, two-pagers, brochures, presentations, and donor-facing marketing materials. Create tailored, engaging multimedia content for CRS global social media platforms (such as LinkedIn, Facebook, X, and Instagram) in coordination with project teams. Ensure all produced materials strictly adhere to CRS graphic identity guidelines and specific donor branding and marking requirements. Provide hands-on communications support for events, including managing signage, producing handouts, capturing event photo/video, and coordinating visibility assets. Develop and distribute simple, practical content collection tools for field staff and partners, such as basic interview templates and photo/video guidance. Provide casual, hands-on technical guidance and basic training to staff and local partners on how to capture quality photos, and stories in the field. Manage relationships with local and national media outlets, identify opportunities to elevate program visibility, and package field content and press materials to support country leadership with external representation and media engagement. Adapt the writing, tone, and messaging of materials to fit the specific needs of different audiences, ensuring all materials are properly formatted and ready for distribution. Required Languages - Strong written and spoken English required. Proficiency in Luganda and other local languages is highly desired. Travel - include percentage of required travel, if applicable. Could be stated as Must be willing and able to travel up to 40 %. Basic Qualifications Bachelor's Degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field, experience with INGOs or UN agencies preferred. Minimum 3 years’ of marketing and communications experience, ideally for an NGO or another organization involved in development and humanitarian programming. Individual must possess the ability to influence without direct authority. Ability and desire to work effectively with diverse staff, partners, and participants in a cooperative and professional manner. Must possess the ability to handle multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Demonstrated track record of successfully developing and disseminating information to a variety of target audiences. High proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and desktop publishing tools is required. Preferred Qualifications Experience in graphic design, photo editing, and producing basic social media videos using the Adobe Creative Suite (especially InDesign, Photoshop, and Premiere Pro) or Canva is strongly desired. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Exceptional relationship management skills, with the ability to navigate high-level partner relationships and engage effectively with stakeholders at all levels, both internally and externally Demonstrated experience of successful program management, leading and coaching diverse, multi-disciplinary teams. Strong strategic, analytical, systems thinking, and problem-solving skills, with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment and decisions. Strong communications and presentation skills, able to develop tailored and persuasive messaging for varied audiences. Supervisory Responsibilities: No Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff): Personal Accountability – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions. Acts with Integrity - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest. Builds and Maintains Trust - Shows consistency between words and actions. Collaborates with Others – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams. Open to Learn – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things. Agency Leadership Competencies: Lead Change – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation. Develops and Recognizes Others – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance. Strategic Mindset – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities. How to apply CRS is an Equal Opportunity Employer: We encourage all qualified candidates to apply for this position, including individuals from marginalized backgrounds and people with disabilities. Please ensure you follow the instructions outlined below when applying. This position is open to Ugandan nationals only . Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm. Applications will only be accepted electronically via the following link: https://eipn.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_1/job/3002926/?utm_medium=jobshare&utm_source=External+Job+Share Please Note: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
